# Anything-to-Journal

Anything-to-Journal is a folder-first agent skill that turns source material into an editable journal manuscript, compiled PDF, audit trail, submission bundle, and local PDF/LaTeX editing workspace.

## Install and update

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

- Install: `npx anything-to-journal@latest install`
- Update: `npx anything-to-journal@latest update`
- Options: `npx anything-to-journal@latest --help`

## Documentation

- /docs — Introduction
- /docs/getting-started — Complete first-run workflow
- /docs/folder-contract — Source workspace contract
- /docs/templates — Draft mode and journal-template mode
- /docs/overleaf — Upload the generated ZIP to Overleaf
- /docs/troubleshooting — Compile, citation, figure, and evidence fixes

## Essential workflow

1. Create a new folder dedicated to one manuscript.
2. Put every relevant source in that folder.
3. Open the agent from inside the folder and invoke Anything-to-Journal.
4. Confirm a flexible journal draft or a specific journal template.
5. Review the generated manuscript and generation report.
6. Open the local Manuscript Workspace to preview the PDF and edit the actual generated LaTeX.
7. Continue revising through Codex chat or manual edits; both routes update the same manuscript files.
8. Run the existing final build and audit, or upload `journal-output/submission/overleaf-upload.zip` with Overleaf: New Project > Upload Project.

The generated ZIP has `main.tex` at its root.

## Manuscript Workspace

- Starts locally with `python scripts/workspace_editor.py <journal-output>`.
- Binds to `127.0.0.1` and does not upload unpublished manuscripts.
- Opens with a scrollable PDF Preview and a LaTeX tab for the real `journal-output/manuscript/manuscript.tex` file.
- Saved edits recompile and refresh the PDF; failed compiles keep the last successful preview.
- Detects external edits made by Codex and protects unsaved browser changes from being overwritten.
- The same localhost URL works in Codex Desktop and a regular browser.

The landing page includes an English / Traditional Chinese language switch. Documentation routes remain in English.
